images.title: Reading between the marks
images.purpose: Show a screw ending between 2 cm and 3 cm on a ruler where the centimetre is split into 10 equal parts, read as 2 7/10 cm.
images.composition: A single ruler runs across the middle with a teal screw above it; the gap between 2 and 3 is the focus with generous white space.
exact_structure: A horizontal ruler with big marks labelled 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 (5 big marks, 4 equal centimetre gaps).
Only the gap between 2 and 3 carries small ticks: 9 small ticks, making 10 equal parts, drawn in grey (#6B7280).
A teal (#0072B2) screw lies above the ruler, its left end at 0 and its tip exactly on the 7th small tick after 2.
The 7 parts after the 2 mark are shaded reddish purple (#CC79A7) as a thin band on the ruler; a short bracket under them is labelled 7 parts.
A short dashed grey vertical line from the screw tip down to the ruler. A label above the tip reads 2 7/10 cm.
rejection: the gap between 2 and 3 is not split into exactly 10 parts
the screw tip is not on the 7th tick after 2
small ticks drawn in gaps other than 2 to 3
any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A length between two marks is read as whole units first, then the tenths after them.
images.description: A ruler marked 0 to 4 with the gap from 2 to 3 split into ten parts and a screw ending at the seventh part.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Count the whole centimetres first, then the small parts after the 2 mark.

image_decisions.why: The image shows why a unit is split into ten parts and how 2 7/10 cm is read.
